correctness.rationale: Positive-height bi-infinite Dyck periodic coding is bijective with M+1-symbol words having j=(n-d)/2 generic closing symbols; exact F_n(d) follows. A k-repeated point has both period and height divisible by k, yielding the gcd(n,d) Mobius formula. The d=1 and d=2 specializations and parity period-half subtraction follow algebraically. Exponential bound for omitted negative heights and shorter repeats, Stirling, and the binomial CLT establish rare-shell prefactors and Gaussian limit. Finite exact enumeration for M=2,n<=10 and M=3,n<=8 agrees for 91 cases; the infinite proof is analytic.
